speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Given your fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph node, I need to determine if this is an infectious process or malignancy. Have you had any recent fevers, or have you noticed any lumps elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very concerning constellation of symptoms, often referred to as "B symptoms." To narrow this down, have you experienced any persistent cough, shortness of breath, or any change in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The presence of painless, fixed supraclavicular lymphadenopathy combined with B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and recent neck swelling is highly suggestive of this malignancy. I recommend a CT scan of the chest and abdomen immediately to stage the disease.
